pattern.short_summary: The interface takes an input the model has already been run on, applies a controlled alteration to it, re-runs the model, and presents the altered-input output against the original one.
pattern.definition: The interface takes an input the model has already been run on, applies a controlled alteration to it, re-runs the model, and presents the altered-input output against the original one. The alteration is authored or parameterized by the user, and its known content is what makes the resulting difference readable. The comparison, not either output alone, is the thing the user is given.
pattern.structural_signature: Control flow: for a held input x, the system constructs one or more variants x' by a user-specified transformation rule (granularity, target, magnitude), executes the same model on x and each x', and joins the outputs into a paired or batched display keyed to the transformation that produced each. The distinguishing structure is that the delta is *induced by the interface* rather than found in the data, so the manipulated dimension is known to the system and can be used as the organizing axis of the display. This transplants: the same signature describes a spreadsheet what-if sweep, a compiler flag sweep, or an injected-decoy audit of a retrieval index.

dimension.category_description: How multiple possibilities are presented, previewed, maintained, blended, or compared before commitment.
dimension.classification_boundary: Requires a visible choice or comparison mechanism, not backend candidate-set processing alone.
